verdict: Uber's trips grew 22% and revenue 20% to $14.4B, with operating profit up 130% to $1.8B — but a $1.6B paper loss on its investment stakes cut reported net income to $317M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: cut by a $1.6B paper loss on investments

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — the original Uber business. Gross Bookings rose 20% to $27.4B.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Food and grocery delivery — Uber Eats and couriers, growing far faster than rides.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking logistics — matching shippers with carriers. Revenue and bookings were flat.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Running the platform day to day — support, operations and local teams.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Promotions, advertising and winning riders, eaters and drivers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform and its autonomous-vehicle partnerships.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, finance and the back office.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of equipment and past acquisitions over their useful lives.

follow100Note: Of the $2.21 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $0.15 belongs to non-controlling partners — $2.06 is Uber shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Bookings still booming
takeaways.text: Gross Bookings grew 22% to $54.1B, with trips up 22% to 3.8 billion and Monthly Active Platform Consumers up 18%. Revenue grew 20% to $14.4B.

takeaways.title: Operating profit more than doubled
takeaways.text: GAAP income from operations rose 130% to $1.8B and Adjusted EBITDA 35% to $2.5B. Free cash flow was $2.8B — the core business had a very strong quarter.

takeaways.title: A paper loss did the damage
takeaways.text: Other expense, net was $1,568M, driven by a roughly $1.6B net headwind (pre-tax) from revaluations of Uber's equity investments. It cut net income to $317M ($296M to Uber shareholders, $0.14 a share), even with a $40M tax benefit helping.

oneTimers: A net loss of roughly $1.6B (pre-tax) from revaluations of Uber's equity investments sits in other income (expense), net — paper losses on the value of stakes Uber holds, not cash lost from rides or deliveries.
otherDetail: Interest income of $200M, less $115M of interest expense, a $1,568M other-expense line — mostly a roughly $1.6B net loss on revaluations of Uber's equity investments — and a $14M equity-method loss.
footerNote: Net income of $317M includes $21M attributable to non-controlling interests; $296M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $0.14 EPS figure). Cost of revenue is shown excluding depreciation and amortization, exactly as Uber reports it. The quarter's $40M income-tax benefit is drawn as money added back at the bottom line.
